# OpenCode Interface Contract

<!-- GENERATED from src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/opencode.contract.ts by scripts/generate-contract-docs.mjs — do not edit. Run `npm run contract:docs`. -->

Every external interface of OpenCode that Cinna relies on, one entry each: what the tool must do, which Cinna code depends on it, and what the user loses when it stops. **Verified against OpenCode CLI 2.0.27** — the version pinned in `src/shared/runtimePins.ts`.

Each entry has exactly one test, titled with its id, in [`opencode.contract.test.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/opencode.contract.test.ts). They run the real pinned binary over stdio against a loopback fake provider — no login, no provider request — with `npm run test:contract` (`make contract ENGINE=opencode` installs the binary first). They are not part of `npm test`.

The raw shapes a run observes are compared with the committed [`opencode-2.0.27.json`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/snapshots/opencode-2.0.27.json), and a difference fails the run; `make contract-snapshot ENGINE=opencode` rewrites it once a change is understood. To evaluate a new release, `make contract-next ENGINE=opencode VERSION=<x.y.z>` runs the same tests against that version without changing the pin; red entries name their owners below, and the run prints the diff between the pinned snapshot and the candidate's (written to a temp path, never into the tree) — that diff is what changed.

Hand-written evidence and reasoning stay in [The ACP Engine Contract](../acp_contract.md) and [The OpenCode Engine Contract](../opencode_contract.md); this file is only the index of what is checked.

**Flow step** names the step of the Level 2 whole flow that exercises the entry — **A** plain chat on the Default runtime, then its title (the engine’s own on Codex, Cinna’s AI title elsewhere); **B** a specialist @-added mid-chat, called through Cinna’s MCP server; **C** continuity: a later turn remembers the first; **D** a specialist attached before the first turn. A dash means no step does, and the note says why. No Level 2 variant walks them for OpenCode: neither the no-billing `e2e/specs/runtime-flow.spec.ts` nor `make live-flow` runs it; the billed live specs are its end-to-end check. The config and environment are the production launcher’s, so the fake provider is an ordinary `openai_compatible` credential. A binary of your own runs the same tests with `CINNA_CONTRACT_OPENCODE=<binary> npm run test:contract -- src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/opencode.contract.test.ts`.

| `opencode.launch.version-output` | CLI: `--version` | Prints `opencode v<version>` on stdout and exits 0; `opencodeMajorVersion` reads 2 from it, and the pinned binary prints exactly the pin’s `versionOutput`. | [`engine.ts`](../../../../src/shared/engine.ts) `opencodeMajorVersion`<br>[`binaryResolver.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/binaryResolver.ts) `acceptsVersion` | Every managed install is discarded as the wrong version, or a configured 2.x is refused as 1.x. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.launch.personal-skills` | file: `opencode.json plugins: -opencode.config.compatibility` | With the launcher’s generated config, a session’s model request lists each kit skill passed by its own folder in `skills.paths` (`cinna-tasks`, `cinna-artifacts`, a root `SKILL.md` each) and none of `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the sandbox HOME; the same config with `plugins: []` lists both personal skills, so their absence is the plugin entry’s doing. 2.0.27 sends `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` in neither session (the snapshot’s `personalWithoutPluginEntry`), so its absence proves nothing about the plugin. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `OPENCODE_NO_COMPATIBILITY_PLUGIN`<br>[`configGenerator.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/configGenerator.ts) `skillPaths` | A Cinna agent silently picks up the user’s personal Claude Code skills and instructions, and an agent shared with a team behaves differently on each member’s machine. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.launch.database` | env var: `OPENCODE_DB` | The session database (`opencode.db`, with its `-wal`/`-shm`) is created at the absolute `OPENCODE_DB` the launcher sets, and none is created under XDG data (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/`). | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `OPENCODE_DB`<br>[`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `opencodeDatabasePath` | Cinna’s sessions are written into, and migrate, the user’s own OpenCode database. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.launch.database-first-start` | CLI: `acp (first starts on a missing OPENCODE_DB)` | Several `acp` planned together by the launcher on an `OPENCODE_DB` that does not exist yet, and started at once, reach `session/new`: the launcher first creates the database with one `acp` stopped once it has answered `initialize`. Without it 2.0.27’s schema bootstrap races and the losers exit with “Standalone server exited before reporting readiness”. No start is lost: concurrent starts still die now and then on `database is locked` at open, and the launcher’s `earlyExitRetry` starts such a process again (up to three spawns, within the start timeout). | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `ensureOpencodeDatabase`<br>[`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `bootstrapOpencodeAcp`<br>[`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `OPENCODE_EARLY_EXIT_RETRY` | The first autorun or delegation burst after an upgrade (or on a new install) loses turns at spawn. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.launch.process-tree` | CLI: `acp (process tree)` | Signalling the `acp` process alone, with SIGTERM and with SIGKILL, ends it and leaves no descendant alive. It runs one child, `serve --stdio`, in a process group of its own, which the group kill does not reach — it exits because its parent went. | [`acpConnection.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpConnection.ts) `killTree` | Stop, a pool eviction or quitting the app leaves an engine server running per chat, holding its session database open. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.session.initialize` | ACP method: `initialize` | Answers protocol version 1 with `loadSession: true`, `mcpCapabilities.http: true` and `mcpCapabilities.sse: false`, so Cinna’s session server must stay `type: "http"`. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `ACP_PROTOCOL_VERSION`<br>[`conductorMcpServer.ts`](../../../../src/main/services/conductorMcpServer.ts) `type: 'http'` | No OpenCode session starts, a resumed chat loses its conversation, or Cinna’s MCP server is never connected. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.config-options` | ACP field: `session/new configOptions` | `session/new` answers `sessionId` and `configOptions` holding the select options `mode`, `model` and `effort` (category `thought_level`). | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `configOptions`<br>[`acpMessages.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpMessages.ts) `selectedModelOf` | The agent’s definition cannot be selected, and the session runs OpenCode’s stock coding agent in the user’s folder. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.set-config-option` | ACP method: `session/set_config_option mode, model` | Setting `mode` to the agent key `buildEngineConfig` named, then `model` to `<provider>/<model>`, both succeed and answer `configOptions`. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `configId: 'mode'`<br>[`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `configId: 'model'` | The turn is refused at setup, or runs on another agent or model than the folder chose. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.system-prompt` | provider request: `agent prompt → system message` | Once `mode` selects the agent, its `prompt` from the generated config arrives in the provider request’s system messages. | [`configGenerator.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/configGenerator.ts) `buildEngineConfig` | A folder agent runs without its instructions. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.load-replay` | ACP method: `session/load` | In a fresh process, `session/load` of a session the previous process created succeeds, replays its history as `session/update`s (user, agent, thought and tool updates), and the next prompt’s request carries the earlier turns. | [`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `session/load` | A chat resumed after an app restart or a process eviction starts from nothing. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.load-unknown` | ACP method: `session/load (unknown session)` | In a process on another database, `session/load` of a session id it has never seen answers a JSON-RPC error, promptly, and replays nothing — the driver then starts a fresh session. | [`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `the remembered ACP session was gone` | A chat whose session lives in another database (the user’s shared one, before Cinna had its own) hangs or errors at its first turn instead of starting fresh. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.thought-message-id` | ACP field: `agent_thought_chunk.messageId` | A streamed reasoning summary arrives as `agent_thought_chunk`; it and the reply’s `agent_message_chunk` both carry the message id (`msg_…`). | [`acpMessages.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpMessages.ts) `agent_thought_chunk` | Thinking is filed under message keys of its own; the turn’s parts are flattened in arrival order, so a change here shows as split or reordered thinking in the transcript. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.session.child-updates` | _meta key: `clientCapabilities._meta["opencode/child-session-updates"] / opencode/session/child_update` | `initialize` answers `agentCapabilities._meta["opencode/child-session-updates"]: true`. With the launcher’s declaration, a `subagent` call (`rawInput {agent, description, prompt}`) opens a child session whose traffic arrives only as `opencode/session/child_update` {rootSessionId = the prompted session, childSessionId, parentSessionId, depth 1, title = the call’s `description`}: `type: "status"` `created`, `running`, then `completed`, and `type: "update"` with the child’s own `session/update` bodies (its reply as `agent_message_chunk`). Nothing of the child is flattened onto the root session, and the call’s final update names the child in `rawOutput.metadata.sessionID` and carries its report. | [`opencodeChildren.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/opencodeChildren.ts) `opencodeClientMeta`<br>[`opencodeChildren.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/opencodeChildren.ts) `OPENCODE_CHILD_UPDATE_METHOD`<br>[`opencodeChildren.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/opencodeChildren.ts) `callOf`<br>[`acpClient.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpClient.ts) `rootSessionId` | Subagents get no activity item and no lane: their tool calls and replies land in the root agent’s own words, or vanish, and nothing shows a subagent running or ending. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.mcp.session-tool` | ACP field: `session/new mcpServers (Cinna’s server)` | Cinna’s server, given as a session `mcpServers` http entry, is reachable. The model sees only Code Mode’s `execute`; its code’s `tools["cinna"].<tool>()` call runs with no ask under the generated profile, and the completed update names it in `rawOutput.metadata.toolCalls`. | [`conductorToolPolicy.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/conductorToolPolicy.ts) `isCodeModeCall`<br>[`conductorToolPolicy.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/conductorToolPolicy.ts) `codeModeCinnaTools`<br>[`configGenerator.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/configGenerator.ts) `CINNA_TOOL_PERMISSIONS` | Delegation, handover and every chat MCP tool are unreachable from an OpenCode agent, or each call asks the user twice. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.mcp.connect-timing` | MCP request: `tools/list after session/new` | A session’s MCP tools are not usable by a first prompt sent the moment `session/new` and its setup have answered — that prompt’s `execute` gets `Unknown tool 'cinna.probe'` — and they are once Cinna’s server has answered the session’s `tools/list` and the launcher’s settle time has passed. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `OPENCODE_MCP_SETTLE_MS`<br>[`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `awaitCinnaTools`<br>[`conductorMcpServer.ts`](../../../../src/main/services/conductorMcpServer.ts) `toolsListed` | The first turn of a chat cannot call Cinna’s tools: a coordinator says it will ask a specialist and never does. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |

## Permissions & questions

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.permission.profile-patterns` | file: `agent permission profile (bash, read)` | Under the conversation profile a shell `ls` runs without an ask and `cat .env` raises one (the secret-file patterns): the config’s `bash` map governs the `shell` tool. A `read` of `.env` (2.x’s `path` argument) is denied by the `read` map without an ask, and the value never reaches the model, while the same `read` of a file no pattern names completes. | [`configGenerator.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/configGenerator.ts) `CONVERSATION_PERMISSIONS`<br>[`configGenerator.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/configGenerator.ts) `SECRET_FILES` | A pattern that misses fails open: an agent reads a secret without asking — or every command asks. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.permission.ask-options` | ACP method: `session/request_permission` | An ask carries `toolCall` with `toolCallId`, `title`, `name`, `kind: "execute"`, `status`, `locations` and `rawInput.command`, and the options `once` (`allow_once`), `always` (`allow_always`) and `reject` (`reject_once`). | [`acpPermissions.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpPermissions.ts) `pickPermissionOption`<br>[`acpPermissions.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpPermissions.ts) `OPENCODE_RESOURCE_FIELDS` | Allow and Deny cannot be answered, or a remembered grant stops matching the command it was given for. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.permission.deny-outcome` | ACP method: `reject_once → session/prompt stopReason` | After Cinna’s `reject_once` the prompt ends `cancelled`, with no further model request. | [`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `DENIAL_CONTINUE_PROMPT`<br>[`acpPermissions.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpPermissions.ts) `pickPermissionOption` | One Deny reads as the user stopping the turn unless the driver continues it. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
| `opencode.question.elicitation` | ACP method: `question → elicitation/create (form)` | The model is offered a `question` tool and, to a client declaring `elicitation.form`, the engine sends `elicitation/create` whose schema has one `q<n>` field per question and a `q<n>_custom` free-text companion; an `accept` with the chosen label reaches the model as the tool’s result. | [`acpQuestions.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpQuestions.ts) `OPENCODE_QUESTION_KEY`<br>[`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `elicitation: { form: {} }` | A question either never reaches the user or asks permission to ask first; a renamed field files an answer under the wrong question. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |

## Provider traffic

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.provider.egress` | network: `HTTPS_PROXY (egress trap)` | Model traffic goes only to the configured loopback `baseURL` (the conversation, and the engine’s own title request, which offers no tools). Every other attempt — all refused by the trap — is to a pinned host: `models.opencode.ai`. A new host fails the run. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE` | A host appearing here is a new place the engine sends something from the user’s machine; one going away can mean a check (catalog, update) Cinna relies on stopped. | — no Level 2 flow runs OpenCode; the billed live specs (`e2e/specs/live*.spec.ts`) cover it end to end |
